newsitem.title: USA: Conrail does not say if meeting to be held.
newsitem.headline: Conrail does not say if meeting to be held.

text.p: An attorney for Conrail Inc told a U.S. District Court judge Tuesday that he was unable to say whether or not a December 23 shareholder meeting would proceed as scheduled.
The meeting is considered critical for a proposed $8.5 billion merger between Conrail and CSX Corp.
"I can't say that at this time," attorney Tom Van Kirk told U.S. Court Judge Donald Van Artsdalen. He was responding to a question from the judge about whether or not the meeting would go forward.

Rival bidder Norfolk Southern Corp has filed suit to block Conrail from postponing the meeting. Conrail is seeking shareholder approval to waive a Pennsylvania law that requires an all-cash payment by CSX, which already has bought 19.9 percent of Conrail in a cash tender offer.
CSX has proposed buying Conrail in a cash and stock transaction. Conrail has rejected a $10 billion all-cash offer from Norfolk Southern.
